subject: augmented model approach to state space models

messages.author: 052dc98fd0a6fd98
messages.subject: augmented model approach to state space models
parts:
Hello,

This is a question on implementing an INLA solution to a state space problem. Your patience would be appreciated as I am not a statistician. 

In many fields, a discrete form of the Verhulst equation is used to model population dynamics. 

A state-space formulation usually involves an observation equation such as: 

(1)  O{t} = q * B{t} 
(2)  B{t+1} = B{t} + r B{t} ( 1 - B{t} / K ) - H{t}  

where:

{t} is time ( in years ) 
O{t} is the observed index of abundance at time {t}, usually with lognormally distributed errors 
B{t} is the unobserved biomass we are trying to estimate, usually assumed to follow a lognormal error distribution 
H{t} is the harvest, usually assumed to be known without error
r is the "intrinsic" rate of increase, usually assumed to be Gaussian 
K is the asymptotic carrying capacity, usually assumed to be Gaussian or Lognormal
q is a proportionality factor, 

Implementation in BUGS is simple. Is it possible to address such problems with the augmented model approach in INLA? If so, would you please point me in the right direction? 

Thank you,
Jae

> (2) B{t+1} = B{t} + r B{t} ( 1 - B{t} / K ) - H{t}

Hi,

the problem is the B(t)^2 term you'll get expanding the last expression,
which is a non-linear term, which we cannot do...

Sorry about this.
